item.title: Pick the Best Ten Seconds

turns.text: Trim this to the best 10 seconds. You pick the part.

item.tests: Tests autonomous highlight selection and an accurate contiguous trim of the supplied video rather than a generated replacement.

answer_sheet.Sound: Keep the original sound from the selected section.
answer_sheet.Crop, text, or other styling: Keep the original framing; no added text or effects.

must_haves: One playable video lasts 10 seconds, within one frame of tolerance.
The output is one continuous excerpt from jet-30s.mp4, with the source framing and playback speed preserved.
The chosen excerpt contains a salient moment of jet action or cockpit interaction, rather than mostly inactive footage.
Original sound from the selected interval remains synchronized; no replacement music, narration, or captions are added.

turns.text: Trim this clip to the best 10 seconds. You pick the part. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**I haven’t run anything or spent any credits.** For a simple trim, you shouldn’t need AI generation.

The connected Magic Hour tools don’t offer a trim-only operation or an exact cost quote. Using the AI video editor would regenerate the footage and consume credits—not just cut it—so I won’t use that without a confirmed price and your approval.

**Cheapest option: $0 and 0 Magic Hour credits.** Trim the original in a free local editor, such as Photos, QuickTime, or iMovie:
- **10 seconds:** retains the original quality; no AI needed.
- **5 seconds:** also free and produces a smaller file.
- **480p export:** reduces file size further, but sacrifices detail.

I can’t preview this attachment through the available tools, so I can’t honestly pick its best 10 seconds yet. Share a viewable preview or timestamped storyboard, and I can choose the strongest start and end points without running a generation.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with the cheapest option you listed

turns.agent:
The cheapest option is **a local trim: $0 and 0 Magic Hour credits**. I haven’t spent any credits.

I can’t perform that trim through the connected tools—they only offer AI processing, not a simple cut. If you have FFmpeg installed, this command saves the middle 10 seconds without re-encoding:

```bash
ffmpeg -ss 10 -i jet-30s.mp4 -t 10 -c copy jet-10s.mp4
```

This uses **0:10–0:20 as a fallback**, not a verified “best” segment, and cuts may shift slightly to a keyframe. If you prefer a point-and-click editor, tell me your device and I’ll give you the shortest steps.
